chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not marry (your daughter) to the son of the paternal uncle and the son of the maternal uncle without their permission.

key_terms.ابْنَ الْأَخِ: Son of the paternal uncle (paternal cousin)
key_terms.ابْنَ الْأُخْتِ: Son of the maternal aunt (maternal cousin)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying two cousins from different uncles simultaneously in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar outlines the condition of 'Ajn' (consent) in the context of simultaneous marriage to cousins, emphasizing the necessity of obtaining permission from both the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the importance of familial harmony and the rights of guardians (Awliya) in marital contracts, ensuring that the union does not cause discord between the two branches of the family. It reflects the broader principle that while marriage is permissible, it must be conducted with consideration for the social and emotional well-being of the extended family network.
